finding.claim: SSRF in /logo: the only validation is a substring check (strings.Contains(raw, "example.io")). It does not parse the URL or check scheme or host, so any URL that contains that string passes, e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?x=example.io, http://attacker.com/example.io, or http://example.io@127.0.0.1:9200/. The server fetches the URL with the default http.Get, which follows redirects. It returns the full response body to the caller. An unauthenticated attacker can reach internal services and cloud metadata and read the responses.
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, with the body copied back to the client at main.go:38

trace.note: strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is the only gate; it is a substring match, not a host check
http.Get(raw) fetches the URL using the default client, which follows redirects and allows any scheme and host
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) returns the response body to the attacker, so the SSRF is non-blind

finding.guards_checked: Substring check on the raw string (bypassable, not an allowlist). No url.Parse, no scheme or host allowlist, no IP or private-range blocking, and no redirect restriction (default client). No auth middleware. The resp error is ignored at line 36, but that only causes a nil-pointer panic and is not a control.

verdict.guard_found: Only strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") at main.go:32, a substring check that does not close the finding. The strict host allowlist and no-redirect client are in the separate /cdn handler (main.go:20-24), not /logo.
verdict.reason: The `logo` form value (main.go:31) is attacker-controlled and passes only the substring check at main.go:32. It then reaches `http.Get(raw)` at main.go:36 on the default redirect-following client. The body is returned to the caller at main.go:38, and the route is unauthenticated (main.go:43).
